messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1782 - p99 latency spike observed for hosted-inference (us-east1) - auto-page triggered. Root cause suspected: KV cache pressure. Please ack and triage.

ryan_l: acked. I'm looking at tracing now — p95 up ~120ms->320ms, p99 spiking ~800ms->2.4s for streaming endpoints. Affected route: /v1/stream and some chat sessions showing stalls.

maya: seeing streaming stalls (client sees no tokens for ~2s) or stalls during decode step? can we confirm if requests are queuing or decode is slow?

jin: attaching quick log snip from runtime nodes (node-12):
```
[2026-03-14T22:04:15Z] WARN runtime.kvcache eviction_start reason=pressure used=0.94 evict_rate=430/s
[2026-03-14T22:04:16Z] ERROR runtime.stream stall session=svc-abc reason=kv_miss_blocked decode_wait=1500ms
[2026-03-14T22:04:17Z] INFO runtime.prefill started model=redwood-13b prefill_inflight=340
```

caroline: looks like classic KV cache fragmentation + eviction storms. Eviction rate high and prefill tasks are contending with decode for memory/IO. We have imbalance: many prefill jobs filling large prefixes while streaming decodes need fast KV lookups — realized gens are competing and causing tail latency.

maya: what are cache hit / eviction stats across pods?

jin: pulled metrics: `kv_cache_hit_rate` ~ 0.72 (down from 0.95 yesterday), `kv_cache_evictions_total` spiked to 1.2M in last 10m, `kv_cache_prefill_inflight` ~ 340, avg fragment_count ~ 480k per shard.

ryan_l: customer impact: 4 paying customers reported degraded streaming (CS ticket ids: CS-4021, CS-4023). No full outages but SLA warnings for Dedicated customers. Escalating to SRE/Support.

sre_pager: notified CS + assigned priority. Reaching out to accounts team for heads-up.

caroline: immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk first):
- reduce `prefill_concurrency` on hosted nodes to lower prefill pressure (hot config)
- increase `kv_cache_eviction_threshold` from 0.7 -> 0.85 to prefer retention of hot entries
- enable `prefill_backoff_on_eviction` flag (experimental) to throttle prefill when evictions high

maya: agree. also consider routing a small % (5-10%) of traffic to a cached-small-model fallback to reduce KV size temporarily. Can do via traffic-routing rules in Console.

ryan_l: applying hot config change to prefill first. Running: `redwoodctl runtime set-config --key prefill_concurrency --value 8 --selector zone=us-east1`

jin: `ack` — I'll watch metrics. If any pod crosses OOM risk we should drain and restart safely.

oncall-bot: update: hot-config change applied by ryan_l at 22:07Z. Prefill concurrency lowered 32->8. Monitoring.

(1m later)
jin: metrics: eviction rate dropped ~60%, p95 back near 140ms, p99 trending down but some residual stalls at 1.1s. Prefill queue length decreased.

caroline: still seeing fragmented KV segments causing occasional GC-like stalls. Longer-term fix: change allocator to favor decode-critical entries (LRU with pinned tokens) and compact fragmented KV segments in background. I have a patch ready for review: PR #3645 - "kv: prioritize decode hotset and background compaction".

ryan_l: can we hotfix config to bias cache pinning toward recent decode keys? Is that toggle-able?

caroline: yes, there is `kv_pin_strategy=recent_decode` in runtime flags. Rolling to 10% of pods as experiment: `redwoodctl runtime set-config --key kv_pin_strategy --value recent_decode --selector canary=true`

maya: also initiating traffic fallback rule to route 8% of traffic for affected routes to `redwood-7b-prefill` model to reduce memory pressure. Will watch customer latency and loss.

jin: rolled canary pin config to 12 pods. Logs show less decode_wait errors on those pods.

(10m later)
ryan_l: p99 overall stabilized to ~820ms -> 420ms, streaming stalls mostly resolved. CS informed. Marking incident as mitigated for now but will keep it active for follow-through.

sre_pager: good work. Please prepare RCA notes and tentative timeline for permanent fix (compaction + allocator change). Also include customer impact summary and commit IDs for hot configs + PR #3645.

caroline: I'll open an incident postmortem draft with timeline + perf graphs. Action items:
- ship PR #3645 and run canary (owner: caroline)
- add automatic prefill throttle when eviction_rate > 0.2 * capacity (owner: jin)
- add alert for `kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio > 0.5` (owner: ryan_l)
- customer comms follow-up (owner: sre/CS)

ryan_l: handing over to maya for night on-call. Handoff notes: incident mitigated, hot-configs applied (prefill_concurrency=8, kv_pin_strategy=recent_decode on canary), watch p99 and eviction metrics for 3h, if eviction_rate rises redeploy canary allocator patch or temporarily route additional traffic to smaller model.

maya: taking handoff. I'll keep a watch window and ping if anything regresses. Thx all. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident 1782 status -> mitigated (22:18Z). Updating paging logs and creating postmortem issue.

---
Summary: KV cache pressure + prefill vs decode imbalance caused eviction storms and tail stalls. Immediate mitigation: throttle prefill, canary pin strategy, traffic fallback; longer-term fixes: allocator prioritization and background compaction.
